verification.note: Traced by reading; not executed. Old stem `movie.ja`, new stem `movie`. subtitle.py:124-128 lists both sidecars and :135 puts `movie.ja.ja.srt` first. Its target (:140) is `movie.ja.srt`, which still exists, so :143-147 skips it. `movie.ja.srt` then moves to `movie.srt`. Final disk: `movie.mp4`, `movie.srt`, `movie.ja.ja.srt`. `_parse_subtitle_filename('movie', movie.ja.ja.srt)` returns None because `ja.ja` fails the regex at :64, so the Japanese track disappears, with only a warning logged. This is the exact inverse of the rename in test_language_suffixed_stem_does_not_depend_on_listing_order, and no test covers it. No file is lost; the track is stranded.

Traced by reading; not executed. Rows `a.mp4` -> `clip_1.mp4` and `clip_1.mkv` -> `clip_2.mkv` pass fileops.py:1041-1060, which compares full names. Step 1: `a.srt` targets `clip_1.srt`, which exists, so subtitle.py:143-147 skips it and `a.srt` stays. Step 2: the earlier row now holds stem `clip_1` (fileops.py:1172-1173), so `clip_1.srt` is shared and copied to `clip_2.srt`, and the original stays (subtitle.py:148-149). `clip_1.mp4` then plays the former mkv's subtitle and `a.srt` has no owner. On the base the wrong track would also be found by stem, so the misattachment itself is not new; stranding `a.srt` and not repairing it are the behaviour of this carry. The known-issues entry at known-issues.md:270 does not describe a sidecar that the same batch is moving away.

Traced by reading; not executed. Batch rename `one.mp4` and `one.mkv` with prefix `x_`: row 1 sees the later row's old stem `one`, so `one.srt` is shared and copied to `x_one.srt`. Row 2 sees only stem `x_one`, so it is not shared, but subtitle.py:143 finds the target and skips before any removal. `one.srt` stays with no owner. Batch move: routers/files.py:395-402 calls move_file per id. The first call sees sibling `one` in the old folder (fileops.py:556, :383-398) and copies. The second call finds no sibling, the target exists, and it skips, so `a/one.srt` stays. test_siblings_renamed_together_share_the_moved_sidecar asserts only `_tracks`. The four test files that use batch/move (test_files_moved_event, test_target_drive_access, test_move_tags_follow_drive, test_lifecycle_ws_events_integration) have no match for srt, vtt or subtitle.

Traced by reading; not executed. init_upload (upload.py:108-151) has no subtitle guard. classify returns (`subtitle`, ...) at filetype.py:260-262, and upload.py:302-316 adds the File row, reached from routers/uploads.py:77. subtitle.py:148-151 moves the file with no database write, and neither carry function in fileops.py updates rows. Limits on the impact: the scanner skips subtitle files before adding to found_paths (scanner.py:451-455), so scanner.py:591 and :768-779 would mark any uploaded subtitle row missing at the next scan even without a carry. The stale active row therefore matters mainly between the carry and the next scan, and a row going missing after a scan is pre-existing. detect_subtitles reads the disk, so the video's track still works. The docs and tests saying subtitles have no rows (viewers-and-players.md:69, routers/drives.py:97-99, test_file_kind_filter.py:219) do not hold for uploads. I did not confirm how such a row renders in the UI.

Traced by reading; not executed. A concrete plan that passes validation: `new.mp4` -> `ep_1.mp4`, `ep_1.mkv` -> `ep_2.mkv`, `ep_2.mp4` -> `ep_3.mp4`. With one extension throughout, the second row would get a 409 from fileops.py:1054, so mixed extensions are required, as the finding says. Row 1: target `ep_1.srt` exists, so skipped and `new.srt` is stranded. Row 2: target `ep_2.srt` exists, so skipped. Row 3: the earlier row's new stem `ep_2` claims `ep_2.srt` (fileops.py:1173), so it is copied to `ep_3.srt`. Final state: `ep_1.mp4` shows the former mkv's subtitle, `ep_2.mkv` shows the former `ep_2.mp4` subtitle, `ep_3.mp4` is correct, and `new.srt` has no owner. The pre-existing note also holds: on the base these names would find the same wrong tracks by stem, because detect_subtitles matches by stem only.

specification_compliance: The carry works for the paths the tests and the R-5 record cover: distinct stems, one video of a same-stem pair, and a growing language-suffixed stem, by tracing the code.

viewers-and-players.md:69 says renaming or moving a video takes its subtitles along. That does not hold for the shrinking language-stem rename, or for batches where a target is still held by a later row, as confirmed in the records above.
potential_unspecified_behavior: A missing row for a video deleted long ago still claims its sidecars through `_sibling_stems`, so a rename copies rather than moves that sidecar. The docstring at fileops.py:384-388 states this on purpose; it is listed only because it also leaves a copy behind.
regression_risks: Reordering sidecars by rename direction, or planning batch moves as a whole, would touch behaviour that has no test today: the batch sibling loop and the disk listing after same-stem batch operations.
Case-only batch renames on a case-insensitive volume leave sidecars under the old case. known-issues.md:264-268 already documents this, so it is not reported as new.
test_coverage: test_sidecar_subtitles_follow_video.py covers the growing language-stem rename in both listing orders, but not the inverse rename.
TestBatchRename has four tests. None has two same-stem rows going to different stems, and the same-destination test asserts `_tracks` only.
No test seeds sidecars through PUT /batch/move, and no test uploads a subtitle and then carries it.
